problem.text: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 86$, and $AC = 97$. A circle with center $A$ and radius $AB$ intersects $\overline{BC}$ at points $B$ and $X$. Moreover $\overline{BX}$ and $\overline{CX}$ have integer lengths. What is $BC$?

steps.title: Where to start: two secants from $C$
steps.body: Draw a diagram. The circle has center $A$ and radius $86$, and $AC = 97 > 86$, so $C$ is outside the circle. Two lines from $C$ cut the circle: line $CB$ meets it at $X$ and $B$, and line $CA$ meets it at a point $D$ between $A$ and $C$ and at the far end $Y$ of the diameter through $D$. A point outside a circle with two secants is exactly the setup for power of a point: $CX\cdot CB = CD\cdot CY$.

steps.title: Turn it into a factoring problem
steps.body: Power of a point gives $CX\cdot CB = 11\cdot 183 = 2013$. Since $CX$ and $BX$ are integers, $CB = CX + BX$ is an integer too, and $X$ lies between $B$ and $C$, so $CX < CB$. So we need a factor pair of $2013$ with the smaller factor equal to $CX$.

your_turn.prompt: Write $2013$ as a product of primes and list its factor pairs.

steps.title: Use the triangle inequality
steps.body: Four pairs are too many, so look for a bound on $CX$. Triangle $ACX$ has $AX = 86$ (a radius) and $AC = 97$.

your_turn.prompt: What does the triangle inequality in triangle $ACX$ say about $CX$?
your_turn.answer: $AX + CX > AC$, so $86 + CX > 97$, which means $CX > 11$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: $CX > 11$ rules out $CX = 1$, $3$ and $11$ (the pair $11\cdot 183$ would also make $BC = AB + AC$, a flat triangle). The only pair left is $CX = 33$, $CB = 61$, and then $BX = 61 - 33 = 28$ is an integer as required. So $BC = 61$. The answer is **(D)**.

wrong_choices.C: $33$ is $CX$, the piece of $BC$ outside the circle, not the whole side. The question asks for $BC = CX + BX$.
wrong_choices.B: $28$ is $BX$, the chord inside the circle. The whole side is $BC = BX + CX = 28 + 33$.
